Restaurant Radar · for vendors to California restaurants and bars

Restaurants and bars applying for a liquor license in your counties, every week.

What you get, and what you don't

You get each application's business name, street address, license type and state file number (a person's name is never shown): enough to drive by, walk in or mail a card. You don't get owner names, phone numbers or emails, and nobody calls the restaurant to confirm anything. That is why it costs $29 and not the $99 a month per trade area that one contact-verified service, preopeningrestaurants.com, quoted as its starting price on October 31, 2026.

For: food and beverage distributors, restaurant-equipment and refrigeration companies, pest control, hood-cleaning, fire-suppression and grease-trap services, linen services, POS resellers and sign shops.

Counts for every county, pending and new, are on the county pages, rebuilt from ABC's daily file. See a real Los Angeles County sample.

What each email holds

One plain email a week, with the same rows as plain-text CSV at the bottom (paste it into a spreadsheet). Each application shows:

  • the business's trade name (DBA) and company name (names of individuals are withheld)
  • the premises address and the license type, in ABC's words
  • ABC's status, quoted, and the ABC file number for ABC's license lookup

Every row is labeled as an application. An application is not an approval or an opening date. Some are withdrawn or denied, and some are a new owner of an existing place. ABC's license lookup usually shows which, but for some applications that are in ABC's daily file the lookup says "No license found"; we list them because the file lists them.

Your first list is everything pending in your counties. ABC's daily file has no filing date, so after that each weekly list shows what's new since the last one, dated by the first daily file it appeared in. We keep a copy of ABC's file every day to do this.

How many new ones a week? In the 7 days to November 13, 2026: Los Angeles County 16, San Mateo 5, San Diego 4, Alameda 4, and Santa Clara 0. Smaller counties are quiet: 20 of the 55 counties with anything pending had no new application between October 31, 2026 and November 13, 2026. Choose up to 3 counties that add up; see every county, updated from ABC's daily file. We began keeping the file on October 31, 2026, so these are single weeks, not averages. If your counties turn out too quiet, the 7-day refund on your first list covers you.

California only, every county, from California ABC's records. Other states: not yet.

The fine print

  • Informational only, not professional advice. We copy ABC's records and don't verify them beyond the official source.
  • Not a consumer report. It may not be used as a factor in eligibility for credit, insurance, employment, housing, or any purpose covered by the Fair Credit Reporting Act.
  • Business records only. We withhold names that aren't clearly a company's, and add no non-public information about anyone.
  • Excluded: hospitals and anything inside them, clinics, nursing, rehab and senior-living facilities, K-12 schools, daycares and children's facilities. We screen by name; the screen can miss a facility without a telling name. University venues serve adults and stay in.
  • We never contact the businesses listed.
  • Source: California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (abc.ca.gov), whose site says its information "is considered in the public domain". We're not affiliated with or endorsed by ABC, and records come "as is".
